'''Lars Bildsten''' (born 1964) is an American [[astrophysics|astrophysicist]], best known for his work on the physics of [[white dwarf|stars, white dwarf]]s and their explosions as [[Type Ia supernova]]e.  He is the sixth director of the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at  [[University of California, Santa Barbara|the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB)]] and a professor in the [[University of California, Santa Barbara Physics Department|UCSB Physics Department]].

==Biography==
Bildsten received a [[Bachelor of Science]] with a major in [[engineering physics]] from [[Ohio State University]] in 1985 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in [[theoretical physics]] from [[Cornell University]] in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lars Bildsten – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/lars-bildsten-iprtqj/ |access-date=2024-10-09 |website=National Academy of Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last1=Bildsten |first1=L. |title=Destruction and excitation of accreted nuclei in neutron star atmospheres: Gamma ray lines and X ray bursts |type=PhD |publisher=Cornell University |year=1991 |bibcode=1991PhDT.........7B}}</ref>

Bildsten was then a research fellow at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] for three years, after which he accepted a faculty appointment at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. Rising from assistant to associate professor, in both the physics and astronomy departments, he moved to UCSB in 1999.<ref name="kitp">Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics, [http://www.kitp.ucsb.edu/bildsten "Lars Bildsten Biographical Sketch"]</ref> In 2010, he was awarded the Wayne Rosing, Simon and Diana Raab chair in theoretical astrophysics. He was named director of the Kavli Institute, succeeding [[David Gross]], in 2012.<ref>Kavli Foundation, [http://www.kavlifoundation.org/kavli-news/kitp/bildsten-appointed-endowed-chair "Astrophysicist Lars Bildsten Appointed to Endowed Chair at Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108062851/http://www.kavlifoundation.org/kavli-news/kitp/bildsten-appointed-endowed-chair |date=January 8, 2018 }}</ref>

In addition to his university teaching and research, Bildsten has devoted significant effort to strengthening science and engineering education in grades 7–12. A member of the board of directors of Santa Barbara's [[Dos Pueblos Engineering Academy]] Foundation, he worked to raise $3 million in funding for a dedicated facility and to support math tutors.<ref>American Physical Society, [http://www.aps.org/about/governance/election/lars-bildsten.cfm "Lars Bildsten, Candidate for Chair-Elect, Nominating Committee"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160514083230/http://www.aps.org/about/governance/election/lars-bildsten.cfm |date=May 14, 2016 }}</ref>

==Honors==
Bildsten received an [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Fellowship]] in 1995.  In 1998, the [[Research Corporation]] designated him as a Cottrell Scholar.  He was awarded the [[Helen B. Warner Prize for Astronomy|Helen B. Warner Prize]] of the [[American Astronomical Society]] in 1999<ref>{{Citation | title = Lars Bildsten received the 1999 Helen B. Warner Prize of the American Astronomical Society. | year = 1999 | journal = Physics Today | volume = 52 | issue = 7 | pages = Q67| bibcode = 1999PhT....52Q..67.| doi = 10.1063/1.2802802}}</ref> and the 2017 [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Astrophysics|Dannie Heineman Prize]].<ref>{{cite web | title=AAS Announces Recipients of 2017 Prizes and Awards | date=January 9, 2017 | url=https://aas.org/posts/news/2017/01/aas-announces-recipients-2017-prizes-and-awards | publisher=American Astronomical Society}}</ref> His invited lectureships include the 2000 [[Edwin Salpeter]] Lecture at Cornell, and the 2004 Biermann Lecture at the Max-Planck Institute for Astrophysics.<ref name="kitp" />
He was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2018 <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/May-1-2018-NAS-Election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501225028/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/May-1-2018-NAS-Election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 1, 2018|title=May 1 2018 NAS Election}}</ref> and Elected a Legacy Fellow of the [[American Astronomical Society]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aas.org/grants-and-prizes/aas-fellows|title=AAS Fellows|publisher=AAS|accessdate=27 September 2020}}</ref>
